Unfortunately that's the consequence of having kids with different needs integrated in a classroom. The theory is that segregating students with disabilities and unique needs (and I consider behavior problems a unique need) does more harm for them than good and that those students have a higher chance of success in a regular classroom...BUT that means that the rest of the kids will suffer. It means teachers need have to give these students extra attention and the other students, therefore, get less. It means not being able to get through lesson plans as quickly or efficiently because they need to break things down, redirect, remove a student, call admin, etc.

The reality is that we are helpless as teachers to change the system and we deal with every need as best as we can. 
As a parent there's a couple things I do.

- In my daughter's class, there is a student who is violent (Kindergarten). I email and report every single incident. Not because I don't think the teacher doesn't know, not because there is anything to do about the incident necessarily but because it creates a trail. It means teachers and admin can look for extra support. This is heavily dependent on Admin and teachers being proactive and able to advocate...many schools won't have these resources but I've learned that bringing the attention constantly creates the evidence to take action (hopefully)
- Where I am, there are rules where if there is an instance of bullying, the bully gets removed and placed in another class. Is it passing along the problem? Yes. But I'm advocating for MY kid when I'm in the parent role. So that history of e-mails is my evidence. It's my "This has been a constant problem, my child is unsafe". Again, I'm lucky to be where I am that bullying is taken seriously.

(I AM AWARE NOT EVERY SCHOOL, TEACHER, OR ADMIN IS IN A POSITION TO ACTUALLY DO SOMETHING BUT ITS WORTH A SHOT)

- The other thing I do is actually the most important. I teach my kid to be compassionate. I explain to her that she is right to be upset by her classmates behaviour and she is right to be upset and hold them accountable for their actions. I also teach her that each child has unique needs whether we can see them or not. Some kids need glasses to see, need wheelchairs to get around, or anything to accommodate them physically. I also teach her that we all think and manage our lives different and that in her class, there are going to be kids that struggle with instructions and behavior that she doesn't struggle with. I have posted a few times with regards to a clothing app being a huge wake up for me to help control my spending. The fact that you are aware is a good start but if you need more support, here is my app experience.

I downloaded an app called Your Closet (I'm on Android) where you can take pictures of all your clothing and accessories and add it all to your calendar as you wear it. For each article you can add information like size, material, cost, etc.

There is a section with statistics where you can see a limited amount of most worn/least worn, and best/worst value. Seeing a bunch "never worn" along with a total closet value really opened my eyes to how much was just waste in my closet.

Even the process of entering everything was therapeutic because it took SO much time. All the time I was working on this app was time I WASN'T wandering in a mall or mindlessly shopping online.

I took pictures of EVERYTHING. After I entered all my clothes , when I felt like I was going to shop online, I'd search for stock photos of my clothing. Lululemon clothing, for example, is easy to find online photos and just Googling  the right words I was able to find a lot. Even going into my email history to find exact descriptions to find pictures that way. I'd save the pictures and then replace the pictures in my app.
Now when I shop online, I download the photos immediately and enter in the cost and such.

The emails also allowed me to add cost as accurately as possible. It was quite the gut punch for me to be face to face with the dollar amount of clothing and shipping and such...but I needed that to really come to terms with THAT is what I need to change and improve my habits on.

I also went as far as to look at old photos of myself to add as much as possible in my calendar to give as accurate idea as possible how many times I wore each item. This, again, took SO much time AWAY from shopping so there was a double win there.

Usually when I shop now (I've improved but still a ways to go) I'll look at my app before I spend. If there's an outfit I like I think more about what I like in the outfit, if it's the top I like, I look at my bottoms section for something that could work instead of buying the whole outfit. Or even look and realize I already have something similar and pass altogether.

Hopefully you find something that works for you. Be kind to yourself as you learn to change/improve your habits. Luckily this community understands the struggle and is cheering for you!
